newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says there must be no delay to EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says there must be no delay to EMU - paper.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that all countries must prepare for a launch of European monetary union on time on January 1, 1999.
"We must all prepare to be there on January 1, 1999. To consider that we do not respect this timetable is to give up on it in advance," he said in an interview with local Lyon newspaper Le Progres.
Arthuis, in Lyon for a meeting between the French and German finance ministers and central bank heads, also said he wanted as many countries as possible to qualify to join the new euro.
And he said he was confident Germany would meet Maastricht treaty criteria for entry to the single currency.
Many private economists say they believe Germany will be unable to reduce its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year, in line with Maastricht treaty requirements.

"There are indeed questions in Germany about its ability to respect the (Maastricht) convergence criteria...Nonetheless I do not doubt the ability of the German authorities to take the necessary measures to meet their commitments," he said.
"Moreover, nor do I doubt the ability of other countries in the European Union, and I want as many countries as possible to qualify for the switch to the euro," he added.
